newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jewish protests over new Le Pen gas chamber remark.
newsitem.headline: Jewish protests over new Le Pen gas chamber remark.

text.p: A French Jewish leader called on Monday for new court action against extreme right politician Jean-Marie Le Pen for repeating a comment that gas chambers were a mere detail of World War Two.

"We condemn this new provocation and hope the French justice system will itself initiate legal action on this provocation," said Henri Hadjenberg, president of the Council of French Jewish Institutions (CRIF), French Jewry's roof organisation.
Hadjenberg, speaking to French radio, was commenting on statements by National Front leader Le Pen in the latest issue of the news magazine The New Yorker.
The Jewish leader also expressed outrage at a comparison Le Pen made between Israeli Prime Minister Benyamin Netanyahu and Adolf Hitler.

The New Yorker asked Le Pen about a comment he made in 1987 saying gas chambers were a detail in wartime history and for which he was subsequently sentenced by French courts to pay heavy damages to war victims' groups.
Le Pen's reply to the American weekly was: "The gas chambers have nothing to do with anti-semitism. When I say that the gas chambers are a detail of the history of the Second World War, it's obvious.

"If you take a book on the Second World War of a thousand pages, you will have four pages on deportation (to concentration camps), and on these four pages you have six lines on the gas chambers," he said.
"If it's the national and patriotic ideology that is the basis of Nazism, then Netanyahu is a super-Hitler," Le Pen said.
Denying being a racist, Le Pen was quoted as saying: "What do I have to do not to be racist? Marry a black woman? With AIDS if possible?"

CRIF said in a separate statement that Le Pen's comments appeared aimed at drawing attention to himself as France seemed headed for a new parliamentary election which President Jacques Chirac was expected to announce later on Monday.
"To get back up there into print, Jean-Marie Le Pen is coming back to one of his favourite themes: Jews," CRIF said.
It said his new statement saying gas chambers were not connected with anti-semitism appeared aimed at legitimising anti-semitism.
Several publications run by influential members of his party are dominated with stories about Jews or Israel written in a way that just skirts strict French anti-discrimination laws.
Le Pen scored nearly 15 percent in the country's 1995 presidential elections and his party is expected to chalk up a similar score if parliamentary elections were held now.
